bib.title: Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering
bib.venue: 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; figure text garbled by font encoding (Fig 1, 15-17 text unreadable, not needed).

question: Can a multimodal science QA benchmark with annotated lectures and explanations show whether language models benefit from generating chains of thought, in fine-tuning and few-shot settings?
hypothesis: Models that generate lectures and explanations as a chain of thought answer better, and learn from less data, as humans do with explanations.
contributions: Build SCIENCEQA, 21,208 multimodal science questions with rich domain diversity and annotated lectures and explanations.
Show CoT benefits large language models in both few-shot and fine-tuning learning by improving performance and reliability via explanations.
Explore the upper bound of GPT-3 with gold explanations and show CoT helps models learn from fewer data.

method.summary: The authors scrape K-12 science questions from IXL Learning, clean them, and release SCIENCEQA. They benchmark heuristic, VQA, UnifiedQA (fine-tuned, with and without CoT output) and GPT-3 (zero-, 2-shot, CoT prompting) with images replaced by captions for the language models. Explanations are scored with BLEU, ROUGE-L, Sentence-BERT similarity and MTurk ratings.
method.task: multimodal multiple-choice science question answering with explanation generation

datasets.name: SCIENCEQA
datasets.size: 21,208 questions; 9,122 different questions; 261 different lectures; 26 topics, 127 categories, 379 skills; 7,803 unique image contexts, 4,651 unique text contexts
datasets.source: IXL Learning open resources, California Common Core aligned; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial research only
datasets.preprocessing: Components extracted by heuristic rules; removed single-choice, faulty and duplicate questions; kept one correct answer where several applied; shuffled options; semi-automated reformatting of lectures/solutions; experts manually revised incorrect annotations; newline \n replaced with \\n for language-model inputs; empty string for missing context; images captioned for language models

models.name: UnifiedQA_BASE / SMALL (and CoT variant)
models.architecture: seq2seq text QA model, fine-tuned to emit answer (+ lecture + explanation for CoT)

models.name: VQA baselines: MCAN, Top-Down, BAN, DFAF, ViLT, Patch-TRM, VisualBERT
models.architecture: VQA models with linear classifier over choice scores

training.objective: VQA baselines: classification over choices; UnifiedQA: text generation of answer (QCM->A) or answer+lecture+explanation (QCM->ALE)
training.steps: UnifiedQA: up to 50k iterations, evaluated every 1k, early stopping patience 3 evaluations
training.seq_len: VQA baselines: max 100 input words or tokens

other.fine-tune protocol: train on train, develop on val, evaluate on test

inference.decoding: GPT-3 via online API, default settings
inference.samples: Fig 7 experiments repeated four times with different in-context example sets (Table 9, seeds 3,5,7,9); Tables 3,5,6,7 use trial 1 only; random chance averaged over 3 trials
inference.prompting: GPT-3: 2-shot in-context examples from train set (peak at 2; Fig 7b tests 1-5), format Question/Options/Context/Answer: The answer is X. BECAUSE: lecture explanation; zero-shot and QCM->A baselines too
inference.retrieval: Dynamic sampling of in-context examples from same topic/category/skill tested (Table 5); default random

parameters.prediction rule: generated text mapped to most similar option

other.note: authors say long lecture/explanation before answer risks hitting max token limit; limit value not stated

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction correct among test questions; for generated text the most similar option is the prediction

metrics.name: BLEU-1/BLEU-4, ROUGE-L
metrics.definition: overlap of generated lecture+explanation with gold

metrics.name: Similarity
metrics.definition: cosine similarity of Sentence-BERT embeddings of two sentences

metrics.name: Relevant / Correct / Complete / Gold
metrics.definition: MTurk majority vote of 3 workers; Gold = relevant, correct and complete

baselines: Blind ablations on Top-Down (Q, CI, QM, QCTM, QCIM)
eval.protocol: Accuracy on 4,241 test questions broken down by NAT/SOC/LAN, TXT/IMG/NO, G1-6/G7-12. Human accuracy: test set split into 425 batches of 10 questions plus 5 train questions as exam, each set of 15 given to 3 workers; workers need >=4/5 exam correct, $0.5 per HIT. Explanation evaluation: batches of 10, 3 workers each, $0.3 per batch, majority vote. Error bars only for GPT-3 CoT in Fig 7 (4 repeats); no significance test.

prompts.purpose: GPT-3 (CoT) prompt format, 1 in-context example then test example

limits: Language models see only a generated caption (max length 16) in place of the image, and captions are poor for diagrams (Fig 17a,b).
Blind studies are run on Top-Down only and omit the answer options; no run removes the caption from GPT-3 or UnifiedQA.
GPT-3 results use one in-context example set (trial 1) for Tables 3, 5, 6, 7; error bars only in Fig 7 over 4 repeats; no significance tests.
CoT gain in few-shot GPT-3 is small (1.20 points); explanations placed before the answer reduce accuracy.
Upper bound uses gold lecture/explanation, so it measures leakage of the solution, not achievable accuracy.
Human accuracy comes from AMT with a qualification exam, not expert baselines.
Dataset is K-12 curriculum from one source (IXL), English, non-commercial licence.
